steps.say: Solid shapes are called 3D shapes. You can hold them.

figure.alt: A cube, a sphere, a cylinder and a cone.

steps.say: A sphere is round all over, like a ball. It can roll.

figure.alt: A solid round shape with one curved face and no flat faces.

steps.say: A cube has 6 flat square faces. It cannot roll.

figure.alt: A solid shape with 6 flat square faces, all the same size.

steps.say: A cylinder has 2 flat faces and 1 curved face. It can roll and stack.

figure.alt: A solid shape with 2 flat circle faces and 1 curved face.

check.prompt: A ball is shaped like which 3D shape?
hints: Think about the shape of a ball.
Imagine holding a ball. Does it have flat faces?
check.explanation: A ball is round all over, so it is shaped like a sphere.

options.why: A cube has 6 flat square faces.
A cone has a flat face and a point.

check.prompt: How many faces does a cube have?

figure.alt: A solid shape with 6 flat square faces, all the same size.

hints: A face is a flat side of the shape.
Count top, bottom, front, back and the two sides.
Count the faces you can see. Then think about the ones behind.
